item.title: Bad Asians
item.description: Lillian Li’s Bad Asians is an insightful examination of how parental and cultural demands can stunt the development of an authentic sense of self and shape the course of one’s life.

item.title: Evil Genius
item.description: Navigating Claire Oshetsky’s Evil Genius is like carrying a fully loaded tray of martinis through a bouncy castle planted in quicksand.

item.title: Family Thai
item.description: Cooking from Arnold Myint’s Family Thai feels like having the charismatic author in the kitchen with you.

item.title: Few Blue Skies
item.description: In Carolina Ixta’s beautifully written tale of a girl who never stops pushing for a better future, she plants the seeds of advocacy, perseverance and hope.

item.title: Fros, Fades, and Braids
item.description: Throughout Fros, Fades, and Braids, Sean Qualls encourages young Black readers to fearlessly adopt their own sense of style and individuality.

item.title: Fustuk
item.description: Readers of Fustuk will be drawn to Robert Mgrdich Apelian’s art, stay for the magical joy throughout and walk away feeling full of familial love, but hungry for delicious food

item.title: Her Last Breath
item.description: What Stephen King did for an empty hotel in The Shining, Taylor Adams does for a treacherous cave in his bracing, breathtaking Her Last Breath.

item.title: Last Seen
item.description: In an age of true crime obsession, Christopher Castellani’s novel Last Seen gives a voice to the spirits of people lost.

item.title: So Old, So Young
item.description: In Grant Ginder’s often funny So Old, So Young, five friends try to sort out whether they’re the same as they once were, or if with age and responsibility they’ve lost the best parts of themselves.

item.title: “There are so many ways a cave can kill you”
item.description: A caving expedition descends into chaos in Taylor Adams’ latest suspense novel, Her Last Breath.
